propositions: Seven decorated pytest fixtures return full copies of os.environ directly or nested in fixture arguments, exposing arbitrary ambient secrets when pytest default long traceback renders those arguments on assertion failure.

Minimal-environment testing confirms that all affected fixture consumers pass with only explicit allowlisted variables (fake-bin-first PATH plus per-fixture declared state/path settings), proving no behavioral dependency on arbitrary ambient keys.

Long traceback output leaks inherited secrets exactly once per fixture when failures occur in test assertions, while short traceback does not and fixture argument replacement alone does not prevent the leak.

Each of the seven fixtures must be refactored to return a fresh mutable mapping containing only its required allowlist (PATH, state paths, and fixture-specific overrides like HEALTH_TIMEOUT or REPL_LOG) instead of dict(os.environ).

A parametrized security oracle with insertion-ordered synthetic sentinels validates that no decorated fixture renders ambient values in long traceback output and regresses to RED when dict(os.environ) is reintroduced.
The fix must preserve mutability of existing per-test environment overrides and maintain subprocess contract explicitness without introducing shared abstraction layers.
